pageTitle: Ethotechnics glossary — Accountable systems, AI governance, and correction terms
pageDescription: Definitions of the terms Ethotechnics uses for delegated authority, correction, contestability, and burden, with scope notes, operational tests, and citations.

changelog.summary: Rewrote category descriptions and scope notes to the current framing, replaced vague or promotional definitions in 89 entries and 109 short definitions, removed unsourced adoption and effect claims, and cut filler words and redundant sentences from 38 entries and 20 short definitions. No term was added, removed, or renamed.
Added Typed Decision Model and Confidence-Gated Execution, cross-linked to the worked example of a decision-model gate on refunds.
Added Decision Threshold, Shaping Hop, and Reason Substitution: the places typed decision models locate authority, shape decisions without making them, and separate the reason from the decision.

Promoted 64 orphaned short definitions to full canonical entries across core concepts, governance, decision states, and anti-patterns, and removed three redundant short definitions (procedural-realism, intake-cinema, legibility-illegibility).

Added Feedback Proximity, Asymmetric-Capacity Restraint, Adaptive Capacity, Compensatory Adaptation, and Corrective Power, aligned the short definition of Ethotechnics with its canonical authority-and-correction framing, and refreshed the glossary's category scaffolding off the earlier moral-system vocabulary.

Added Insulation, the unifying failure mode of the framework: whatever stops the consequences of institutional decisions from traveling back to those who can revise the generating rules, with its channels, its good and bad forms, and its self-ratifying loop.

Added Non-Finality, Consequential Contradiction, and The Excluded Case, and generalized the falsified denominator into the falsified ledger — completing the five concerns and the fallibilist ground they stand on.

Added Human Non-Substitutability, Safe Incompleteness, Anti-Conversion Rights, Abstention, Constitutional Debt, Discretion Migration, and Corrigibility Rent — the person-side principles, the three abstentions, and the rent concept.

Added Exception Absorption, Exception Learning, Case Corrigibility, Structural Corrigibility, Institutional Learning, Corrective Debt, and the Workaround Presumption, formalizing the historical turn: reading institutions through their failure trajectories rather than their stated controls.

Added Residual Complexity, Complexity Displacement, Falsified Denominator, Closure Without Remainder, Constitutional Governance, and Post-Optimization Rigor, embedding the foundational contention of burden redistribution.
Added Attestation, Liability Record, Carve-Out, Delegation Chain, Composed Latency, and Silent-Harm Discovery, each bound to the standard clause that requires it.
Added The Non-Conversion Principle, Exit Cost, and Jurisdictional Path Dependence, each linked to the theory essay that argues for it.
Expanded scholarly metadata, operational tests, and provenance notes.
Initial glossary release with stable permalinks.

categories.heading: A. Core concepts
categories.descriptionHtml: Terms that define the discipline: its unit of governance, and the coupling of authority, evidence, capability, consequence, and correction it maintains.

entries.title: Ethotechnics
entries.bodyHtml:
Ethotechnics is the engineering discipline concerned with keeping authority, evidence, capability, consequence, and correction coupled tightly enough that increasing machine agency does not silently become unreviewable institutional power. Where ethics asks “What should we do?”, Ethotechnics designs the mechanisms that make it reliably happen.

Its unit of governance is the consequential decision and the delegated agency that produced it, and its working question is whether that delegation is still a justified delegation today. The method states the chain, the six state variables, and the twelve laws that the standards bind.
examples: A hospital release board requires consent checks, stop controls, and named repair owners before deploying triage updates.
entries.scope: A. Core concepts. Terms that define the discipline: its unit of governance, and the coupling of authority, evidence, capability, consequence, and correction it maintains.
operationalTests: Documentation maps each obligation to a mechanism (stoppability, contestability, repair ownership).
Teams can show a shipped feature whose halt, reversal, and appeal paths were designed, measured, and revised.
entries.genealogy: Draws on ethics, safety engineering, and systems design, and judges governance, product, and operations by what their controls observably do.

entries.title: Moral Behavior (of Systems)
entries.bodyHtml: Observable system outcomes that prevent harm, distribute burden fairly, and keep people able to contest and recover. Moral behavior is evaluated via MPIs like time-to-halt, reversibility, and fair burden distribution—not by stated intent. A system does not “behave morally” if MPIs are tracked but do not trigger pause rules, remediation, or resourcing.
examples: A payments platform slows risky recommendations, surfaces a human review queue, and documents reversals when fraud indicators spike.
entries.scope: A. Core concepts. Terms that define the discipline: its unit of governance, and the coupling of authority, evidence, capability, consequence, and correction it maintains.
operationalTests: MPIs are tracked and drive operational thresholds or pause rules.
Post-incident reviews tie outcomes to system controls rather than intent statements.
entries.genealogy: Defines the observable outcomes Ethotechnics checks for across governance, design, and operations.

entries.title: Ethical Load Path
entries.bodyHtml: The traceable chain of authority, decisions, and controls that carries responsibility for outcomes through a system. A clear ethical load path names who can stop, reverse, or repair harm at each stage, linking design authority, oversight horizons, and the repair log so handoffs remain accountable.
examples: A transit authority publishes a named escalation map for halting automated dispatch, including after-hours owners.
entries.scope: A. Core concepts. Terms that define the discipline: its unit of governance, and the coupling of authority, evidence, capability, consequence, and correction it maintains.
operationalTests: Each lifecycle stage has a named owner with authority to stop, reverse, or repair, plus backup coverage.
Incident reviews show the escalation path was used without dead ends or orphaned decisions.
entries.genealogy: Adapts engineering load paths to accountability so responsibility stays traceable across handoffs.

entries.title: Ethotechnic Audit
entries.bodyHtml: A structured assessment of whether a system has the capabilities it needs: stoppability, reversibility, burden distribution, contestability, and accountability. Ethotechnic audits validate evidence, stress-test pathways, and define remediation steps with named owners.
examples: After a harmful rollout, a platform audit verifies stop controls, reversal paths, and repair ownership before relaunch.
entries.scope: A. Core concepts. Terms that define the discipline: its unit of governance, and the coupling of authority, evidence, capability, consequence, and correction it maintains.
operationalTests: Audit evidence includes drills, logs, and user-facing pathways for contesting and repairing harm.
Remediation plans are time-bound, assigned to owners, and re-audited after major changes.
entries.genealogy: Builds on safety and compliance audits while centering harm prevention, repair, and accountability.

entries.title: Conviviality
entries.bodyHtml: The degree to which tools and institutions expand people’s agency, cooperation, and right of refusal instead of enclosing them. Convivial systems keep permission surfaces wide, make opting out safe, and let communities shape the service.
examples: A mutual aid platform lets neighbors pause notifications or change delivery preferences without losing access to support.
entries.scope: A. Core concepts. Terms that define the discipline: its unit of governance, and the coupling of authority, evidence, capability, consequence, and correction it maintains.
operationalTests: People can refuse or change terms without losing core access or being penalized.
Interfaces surface shared control settings instead of only provider defaults.
entries.genealogy: Extends human-centered design by requiring that agency and refusal survive as a service grows.

entries.title: Ethotechnic Maturity
entries.bodyHtml: A developmental scale describing how consistently a system embodies Ethotechnic capabilities across its lifecycle. Early maturity focuses on stopping acute harms; later stages add graceful degradation, contestability, and routine care retrospectives. Mature systems publish SLJs, maintain repair capacity, and review their halt, reversal, and appeal metrics on a fixed cadence.
examples: A rail operator publishes service-level justice metrics, runs quarterly pause drills, and funds dedicated repair staffing.
entries.scope: A. Core concepts. Terms that define the discipline: its unit of governance, and the coupling of authority, evidence, capability, consequence, and correction it maintains.
operationalTests: A maturity level is documented with evidence for each capability and reviewed after major releases.
Maintenance and repair staffing, budgets, and tools are recurring, not ad hoc.
entries.genealogy: Adapts maturity modeling to the order in which a system acquires stop, repair, and appeal capabilities and keeps them funded.

entries.title: Legibility
entries.bodyHtml: How understandable a system’s actions, reasoning, and ownership are to the people affected by it. Legibility complements explainability for accountability and transparent design authority so people can find who decided, why, and how to respond. Legibility is discoverability of who/why/what-next; it does not guarantee the system can be changed.
examples: Residents receive a plain-language notice that names the office, rule, and appeal path behind a zoning decision.
entries.scope: A. Core concepts. Terms that define the discipline: its unit of governance, and the coupling of authority, evidence, capability, consequence, and correction it maintains.
operationalTests: Decision notices include a plain-language rationale, owner, and next step for contesting.
Affected people can reach the policy basis and escalation path within a single click or call.
entries.genealogy: Moves transparency from disclosure to an understanding the affected person can act on.

entries.title: Sociotechnical Alignment
entries.bodyHtml: Alignment achieved across tools, interfaces, incentives, workflows, and organizational structures, as well as in the model. Sociotechnical alignment keeps the ethical load path intact under pressure.
examples: Policy, tooling, and incentives all enforce the same stoppability rules.
entries.scope: A. Core concepts. Terms that define the discipline: its unit of governance, and the coupling of authority, evidence, capability, consequence, and correction it maintains.
operationalTests: Incentives and KPIs reinforce the system's stop, reversal, and repair requirements rather than undermining them.
Incident reviews can trace breakdowns between policy intent and operational tooling.
entries.genealogy: Bridges organizational design and system behavior so that stated intent survives into operation.

entries.title: Delegated Agency
entries.bodyHtml:
The capacity to act with consequence on an institution's behalf, held by a machine, a human, or an assembly of both. Delegated agency is created by an authority grant and exercised through a decision system; it is not a property of the model that happens to be running.

It matters because agency is the quantity that accumulates. An institution that tracks capability but not delegated agency cannot say how much of its consequential action it has handed over, or whether it still holds the correction capacity to take any of it back. Agency handed over under a revisable delegation can be taken back one grant at a time; agency handed over without one comes back only by rebuilding what replaced it.
entries.scope: A. Core concepts. Terms that define the discipline: its unit of governance, and the coupling of authority, evidence, capability, consequence, and correction it maintains.
operationalTests: The institution can list, for one workflow, every action class a machine may take on its behalf.
Each listed action class traces to a named grant holder rather than to a team or a system name.
Growth in delegated action classes over a quarter is reported alongside growth in correction capacity.
entries.genealogy: Names the object the twelve laws govern: not the model, but the agency an institution has handed to it.

minimumEvidence.artifact: A register of action classes a machine may perform on the institution's behalf, with holders.
minimumEvidence.behavior: A new action class appearing only after an authorization decision, visible in the register history.
minimumEvidence.metric: Count of authorized action classes per workflow, tracked against correction capacity over time.

entries.title: Consequential Decision
entries.bodyHtml:
A decision that changes someone's access, money, obligations, safety, or standing, and that the institution would have to answer for. The consequential decision is the unit of governance in Ethotechnics: each one is a link in the chain from evidence to authority to consequence to correction.

Naming the unit matters because it fixes where the governance load sits. Systems governed at the level of the model leave the decisions themselves unaccounted for, which is where unowned harm collects and where prospective auditability has to be designed in.
entries.scope: A. Core concepts. Terms that define the discipline: its unit of governance, and the coupling of authority, evidence, capability, consequence, and correction it maintains.
operationalTests: The system declares which of its outputs are consequential decisions and which are not.
Each consequential decision emits a record naming the evidence, the grant, and the responsible holder.
A person affected by one can obtain that record without filing a formal request.
entries.genealogy: Ethotechnics takes the consequential decision, rather than the model or the product, as the unit that standards, mechanisms, and evals attach to.

minimumEvidence.artifact: A decision record schema listing evidence refs, grant id, holder, and consequence class.
minimumEvidence.behavior: A decision reconstructed months later from its record alone, without asking the team.
minimumEvidence.metric: Share of consequential decisions that emit a complete record, sampled monthly.

entries.title: Decision System
entries.bodyHtml:
The assembled machinery that produces a consequential decision: models, rules engines, queues, humans, policies, and the data they read. Ethotechnics governs the decision system rather than any one component, because the same substrate-independent questions apply whichever part made the call, and the deployment is classified by its substrate profile rather than by which component is fashionable.

It matters because component-level assurance does not compose. A verified model inside an unaudited decision system still produces decisions no one can reconstruct, which is why assurance is tagged with the evaluation layer it holds at, and why reconstructing a past decision depends on prospective auditability designed into the system.
entries.scope: A. Core concepts. Terms that define the discipline: its unit of governance, and the coupling of authority, evidence, capability, consequence, and correction it maintains.
operationalTests: A diagram names every component that can alter a decision, including humans and lookup tables.
Assurance claims state which component they cover and which they do not.
Changing any component triggers review of the decision system, not only of that component.
entries.genealogy: Generalizes the agent safety object model so that a rules engine, a human reviewer, and a model are governed by the same primitives.

minimumEvidence.artifact: A component inventory for one decision path, with the alteration each component can make.
minimumEvidence.behavior: An assurance claim rejected for covering a component rather than the decision system.
minimumEvidence.metric: Share of decision paths with a current component inventory.

entries.title: Justified Delegation
entries.bodyHtml:
A delegation whose authority, evidence, and correction capacity are all currently in force: the grant sits in an allowed grant state, the policy record it rests on has not expired, and the institution can still meet its correction obligation. Justification is a present-tense property, not a fact about the launch review.

It is the point-in-time test. Revisable delegation is the standing property it tests for: the grant stays tied to the evidence that justified it, so it can be narrowed or withdrawn when that evidence changes. Ask whether a delegation is justified to grade it today; ask whether it is revisable to know whether the answer can be acted on at all.

It matters because most delegations fail by outliving their justification rather than by being wrong at the start. Asking whether a delegation is justified today is the operational form of treating authority as an authority lease.
entries.scope: A. Core concepts. Terms that define the discipline: its unit of governance, and the coupling of authority, evidence, capability, consequence, and correction it maintains.
operationalTests: For any decision, the institution can show the grant was in an allowed state at the time it was made.
Every grant names the policy records it depends on, and each has an unexpired validity date.
A grant whose evidence basis has lapsed cannot authorize action until it is renewed.
entries.genealogy: Compresses Laws II and III into a single testable question about the present state of a delegation rather than the quality of its original approval.

minimumEvidence.artifact: A grant record with state, evidence basis, expiry, and renewal basis fields populated.
minimumEvidence.behavior: An action refused because the grant authorizing it had lapsed into review_required.
minimumEvidence.metric: Share of consequential decisions taken under a grant that was in an allowed state.
minimumEvidence.threshold: Target 100 percent; any exception is an incident.

examples: A claims triage delegation is suspended automatically when the population-drift policy record passes its review date, and resumes only after a fresh drift study is filed.

entries.title: Mechanism-first Analysis
entries.bodyHtml:
An approach to evaluating institutions that prioritizes system mechanics—defaults, authority, clocks, and reversibility—over declared values or intentions, because mechanics determine outcomes under load. A statement of values changes nothing until it is backed by an ethical load path and enforceable design authority.

It is the methodological twin of architecture over values: where that claim says structure outranks intent, mechanism-first analysis says to begin the audit at the structure.
entries.scope: A. Core concepts. Terms that define the discipline: its unit of governance, and the coupling of authority, evidence, capability, consequence, and correction it maintains.
operationalTests: An audit opens with the mechanism inventory (defaults, clocks, escalation, reversal) rather than the value statement.
A proposed change is scored by which enforceable mechanism it alters, not by how it is described.
entries.genealogy: Names the reading order Ethotechnics applies to institutions: mechanics first, declared values second.

entries.title: Architecture over Values
entries.bodyHtml: The claim that “ethical” outcomes depend less on what institutions say they value and more on the enforceable structure of how decisions are made and reversed. Values without machinery are aspiration; contestability, reversibility, and stoppability are the machinery.
entries.scope: A. Core concepts. Terms that define the discipline: its unit of governance, and the coupling of authority, evidence, capability, consequence, and correction it maintains.
operationalTests: A value statement traces to a named mechanism that enforces it under load.
Two institutions with identical value statements remain distinguishable by their decision and reversal structures.
entries.genealogy: The working premise behind mechanism-first analysis and the standards’ focus on grants and clocks over mission language.

entries.title: State + Clocks Model
entries.bodyHtml:
A way of seeing power as state transitions plus time: who can change state, how quickly, and whether reversal is time-bound. The model reduces governance to two questions—what is the clock on each state, and who holds the binding clock?

It is the shared notation behind clock-start and clock mismatch and the reversal SLA.
entries.scope: A. Core concepts. Terms that define the discipline: its unit of governance, and the coupling of authority, evidence, capability, consequence, and correction it maintains.
operationalTests: Every decision state has a named owner and a named clock.
The gap between execution speed and reversal speed is measurable, not assumed.
entries.genealogy: Distills the coercion vocabulary into a minimal model of state, owner, and clock.

entries.title: Contestability Architecture
entries.bodyHtml:
The set of design features that make contestation real: decision objects, clock-start, binding authority, evidence parity, and guaranteed override paths.

Contestability is not a sentiment; it is this architecture. Where any element is missing, contestability becomes theater.
entries.scope: A. Core concepts. Terms that define the discipline: its unit of governance, and the coupling of authority, evidence, capability, consequence, and correction it maintains.
operationalTests: Every appealable decision has a decision object, a clock, a binding authority, and a defined override path.
A gap in any one of the five elements is treated as a defect, not a preference.
entries.genealogy: Condenses the contestability requirements into a named checklist of design features.

entries.title: Control Loops (Constraints Framing)
entries.bodyHtml: A safety lens where governance is modeled as feedback: detect harm, trigger intervention, enforce constraints, and learn. Useful for translating Ethotechnics into engineering terms—stoppability becomes a trip wire, ethical interrupts become the actuator, and time-to-halt becomes the latency budget.
entries.scope: A. Core concepts. Terms that define the discipline: its unit of governance, and the coupling of authority, evidence, capability, consequence, and correction it maintains.
operationalTests: A harm signal maps to a named intervention with an owner and a deadline.
A constraint, once tripped, changes system behavior rather than only logging.
entries.genealogy: Bridges the governance vocabulary to control-systems engineering so it can be implemented.

entries.title: Reciprocal Accommodation
entries.bodyHtml:
Reciprocal accommodation is the requirement that an institution adapt its operational cadence, procedures, and expectations to human biological, cognitive, and social constraints, rather than forcing human participants to continually absorb friction and mutilate their own capacities to preserve an unviable operating model.

Where extractive cannibalism treats human reserves as a free shock absorber, reciprocal accommodation treats human frailty, rest, and development as structural invariants that the technical architecture must accommodate.
examples: An automated case intake system pauses assignments and re-routes load when caseworker shift logs indicate consecutive hours without required rest.
entries.scope: A. Core concepts. Terms that define the discipline: its unit of governance, and the coupling of authority, evidence, capability, consequence, and correction it maintains.
operationalTests: The institution tracks recovery and fatigue boundaries for frontline operators and sheds load when thresholds are reached.
Unforeseen edge cases route to supervisory assistance queues rather than extending operator shifts off-ledger.
entries.genealogy: Rooted in occupational health, disability justice, and cybernetic Ashby equilibrium, measuring whether systems adapt to humans or coerce them.

categories.heading: B. Failure modes (why Ethotechnics exists)
categories.descriptionHtml: Recurring ways responsibility dissolves, authority drifts from its evidence, and harm lands on people with no route to challenge it.

entries.title: Moral Latency
entries.bodyHtml: The lag between harm occurring and the system detecting or responding to it. Automation can scale impact faster than oversight, so moral latency demands velocity friction and ethical interrupts that shrink response time.
examples: A clinic triage chatbot keeps routing patients while harm reports queue for hours, delaying escalation.
entries.scope: B. Failure modes (why Ethotechnics exists). Recurring ways responsibility dissolves, authority drifts from its evidence, and harm lands on people with no route to challenge it.
operationalTests: Time-to-detect harm exceeds time-to-scale the impact.
Harm alerts are not tied to pause, rollback, or escalation controls.
entries.genealogy: Applies latency thinking to harm detection so response windows stay tight.

entries.title: Accountability Diffusion
entries.bodyHtml: Responsibility spreads across teams, vendors, and incentives until no one can intervene. Accountability diffusion erodes design authority and leaves harm without a decisive owner. If no one can unilaterally stop or reverse the harm, accountability is diffused.
examples: A support ticket bounces between a vendor and a hospital compliance team, and no one has authority to pause the rollout.
entries.scope: B. Failure modes (why Ethotechnics exists). Recurring ways responsibility dissolves, authority drifts from its evidence, and harm lands on people with no route to challenge it.
operationalTests: Escalation maps lack a single owner with authority to stop or repair.
Incident reviews show repeated handoffs without a clear decision point.
entries.genealogy: Names the structural cause of unowned harm in complex institutions and supply chains.

entries.title: Extraction
entries.bodyHtml: When a system pulls value—data, attention, labor, or social capital—without returning care, consent, or repair. Extraction hides true costs through externalization and steep burden gradients, hollowing trust.
examples: A data-labeling program offloads unpaid overnight verification to gig workers while the platform reports clean metrics.
entries.scope: B. Failure modes (why Ethotechnics exists). Recurring ways responsibility dissolves, authority drifts from its evidence, and harm lands on people with no route to challenge it.
operationalTests: Value metrics are tracked without corresponding burden or consent metrics.
Unpaid or unacknowledged labor is required to keep the system functioning.
entries.genealogy: Frames value capture as a moral risk as well as an economic one.

entries.title: Extraction by Endurance
entries.bodyHtml: Systems that rely on workers or users absorbing fragility through burnout, emotional labor, or unpaid cognitive work—often mislabeled as “resilience.” Ethotechnic practice aims to invert this burden with fair burden distribution.
entries.scope: B. Failure modes (why Ethotechnics exists). Recurring ways responsibility dissolves, authority drifts from its evidence, and harm lands on people with no route to challenge it.
operationalTests: Sustained service quality depends on overtime, heroics, or unpaid labor.
Reported stability drops when people stop compensating for failures.
entries.genealogy: Calls out resilience narratives that mask structural fragility.

entries.title: Drift (System Drift)
entries.bodyHtml: The tendency of systems to drift toward harm over time when incentives, data, or constraints shift. Without protective friction and moral performance indicators, drift quietly erodes safeguards and accountability.
entries.scope: B. Failure modes (why Ethotechnics exists). Recurring ways responsibility dissolves, authority drifts from its evidence, and harm lands on people with no route to challenge it.
operationalTests: Performance metrics improve while harm or complaints trend upward.
Controls are not reviewed when data, vendors, or policies change.
entries.genealogy: Warns that stability requires ongoing recalibration as systems evolve.

entries.title: Externalization
entries.bodyHtml:
Pushing risk, cost, or harm onto other teams, communities, or the future so internal metrics look clean. Externalization appears as pollution, shadow labor, or brittle dependencies outside audits.

Ethotechnics counters it with oversight horizons, MPIs, and transparent repair logs.
entries.scope: B. Failure modes (why Ethotechnics exists). Recurring ways responsibility dissolves, authority drifts from its evidence, and harm lands on people with no route to challenge it.
operationalTests: Costs show up in downstream teams without corresponding resources or ownership.
Audits exclude dependencies where harms are reported.
entries.genealogy: Names the gap between local optimization and systemic responsibility.

entries.title: Brittleness
entries.bodyHtml: When a system fractures under ordinary variance (unexpected inputs, refusals, or edge cases) and people have to absorb the impact. Brittleness signals missing soft edges, thin graceful degradation, and poor refusal tolerance.
examples: A flight booking bot fails on hyphenated surnames, forcing agents to rebook travelers at the counter.
entries.scope: B. Failure modes (why Ethotechnics exists). Recurring ways responsibility dissolves, authority drifts from its evidence, and harm lands on people with no route to challenge it.
operationalTests: Small input variance triggers hard failures instead of safe fallbacks.
Human operators routinely patch failures without tooling support or documented playbooks.
entries.genealogy: Highlights the need for soft edges, graceful degradation, and refusal tolerance.

entries.title: Optimization Myopia
entries.bodyHtml: Metric chasing that narrows attention to throughput or growth while ignoring MPIs. Myopic optimization erodes contestability, raises failure load, and often fuels extraction.
entries.scope: B. Failure modes (why Ethotechnics exists). Recurring ways responsibility dissolves, authority drifts from its evidence, and harm lands on people with no route to challenge it.
operationalTests: Success metrics improve while contestability or reversibility degrades.
Teams cannot state what an optimization costs affected people, or do not track MPIs.
entries.genealogy: Warns against single-metric tuning that crowds out halt, reversal, and burden measures.

entries.title: Precision Laundering
entries.bodyHtml: Using detailed metrics or probabilistic scores to disguise inequity as objectivity. Precision laundering hides burden gradients and externalization behind statistical gloss, undermining explainability for accountability and meaningful contestation.
entries.scope: B. Failure modes (why Ethotechnics exists). Recurring ways responsibility dissolves, authority drifts from its evidence, and harm lands on people with no route to challenge it.
operationalTests: High-confidence scores are presented without error bounds, provenance, or contestability paths.
Appeals are dismissed because numeric outputs are treated as unquestionable despite uneven impacts.
entries.genealogy: Calls out false certainty in quantified systems and the misuse of precision as legitimacy.

entries.title: Compliance Collapse
entries.bodyHtml: When rigid policy checklists replace judgment, causing teams to follow rules while harm worsens. Compliance collapse occurs when design authority is weak and contestability is low, leaving no path to pause or repair.
entries.scope: B. Failure modes (why Ethotechnics exists). Recurring ways responsibility dissolves, authority drifts from its evidence, and harm lands on people with no route to challenge it.
operationalTests: Teams meet checklist requirements but still cannot stop or reverse harm.
Escalations stall because procedures lack discretionary authority or override lanes.
entries.genealogy: Warns when compliance becomes a substitute for judgment and accountability.

entries.title: Ethics Debt
entries.bodyHtml: The accumulation of unresolved ethical risk from shipping capabilities faster than governance, ownership, and repair mechanisms. Ethics debt grows when maintenance debt outpaces the repair log and risks remain unfunded.
examples: A recommender launches without consent review, adding unresolved risks to the repair log backlog.
entries.scope: B. Failure modes (why Ethotechnics exists). Recurring ways responsibility dissolves, authority drifts from its evidence, and harm lands on people with no route to challenge it.
operationalTests: Open ethical risks outnumber resourced remediation plans and owners.
New launches add obligations without increasing repair capacity or budget.
entries.genealogy: Frames ethical risk as a backlog that compounds without investment.

entries.title: Unowned Harm
entries.bodyHtml: Negative outcomes for which no clear individual or role is accountable, even though the system caused them. Unowned harm signals accountability diffusion and weak traceable ownership.
examples: Denied applicants cannot identify a responsible team to contest a decision or request reversal.
entries.scope: B. Failure modes (why Ethotechnics exists). Recurring ways responsibility dissolves, authority drifts from its evidence, and harm lands on people with no route to challenge it.
operationalTests: Affected people cannot find a named owner or appeal path within the product.
Incident reviews conclude with no accountable role assigned or funded repair.
entries.genealogy: Names the gap left when a system causes harm and no role is accountable for it.

entries.title: Capability Overhang
entries.bodyHtml: When a system’s power exceeds the maturity of its controls, making failures likely even without malicious intent. Capability overhang shows up as strong automation but weak stoppability or reversibility.
examples: A model can auto-approve loans, but rollback and auditing are manual and slow.
entries.scope: B. Failure modes (why Ethotechnics exists). Recurring ways responsibility dissolves, authority drifts from its evidence, and harm lands on people with no route to challenge it.

entries.title: Ethics Theater
entries.bodyHtml: Public displays of ethical concern without operational mechanisms that change system behavior. Ethics theater often masks compliance collapse and low contestability.
examples: The team publishes a code of ethics but lacks monitoring or a repair log.
entries.scope: B. Failure modes (why Ethotechnics exists). Recurring ways responsibility dissolves, authority drifts from its evidence, and harm lands on people with no route to challenge it.
operationalTests: Ethics artifacts exist, but there are no operational stop, contest, or repair mechanisms behind them.
Incident reviews cite policy language but show no evidence the policy was enforced.
entries.genealogy: Highlights performative governance that substitutes for real accountability.

entries.title: Authority Drift
entries.bodyHtml:
The gap that opens when what a system does moves away from what its authority grant permits or what its evidence supports. Drift arrives through added integrations, widened inputs, quietly raised thresholds, and habits that outlive the exception that created them, and it accumulates through the automation ratchet.

It matters because every individual step looks too small to review. Drift is detected by comparing observed action classes from capability discovery against grant scope, and it is what justified delegation and the authority lease exist to catch.
entries.scope: B. Failure modes (why Ethotechnics exists). Recurring ways responsibility dissolves, authority drifts from its evidence, and harm lands on people with no route to challenge it.
operationalTests: Observed action classes are reconciled against grant scope on a stated cadence.
Exceptions granted during incidents carry an expiry and are reconciled after the incident closes.
A widening that no one authorized appears in the reconciliation report rather than in a postmortem.
entries.genealogy: Names the drift Laws I, II, and XI describe, in the form an auditor can measure: observed behavior minus authorized scope.

minimumEvidence.artifact: A reconciliation report listing observed action classes not covered by any live grant.
minimumEvidence.behavior: An unauthorized integration disabled after appearing in reconciliation.
minimumEvidence.metric: Count of ungrounded action classes per reconciliation cycle, trended.
minimumEvidence.threshold: Target zero; any non-zero count opens a review.

entries.title: Automation Ratchet
entries.bodyHtml:
Scope growth by accretion, where each extension of an automated system is too small to trigger review and no single step is the one that widened the delegation. The ratchet turns one way only: successful operation is read as licence to extend.

It matters because the end state bears no relation to what was originally justified and no single decision can be pointed at. The countermeasure is to make each widening an expansion decision, which is also what keeps authority drift from being invisible.
entries.scope: B. Failure modes (why Ethotechnics exists). Recurring ways responsibility dissolves, authority drifts from its evidence, and harm lands on people with no route to challenge it.
operationalTests: Scope changes are logged against the grant, however small, with a cumulative view available.
A cumulative threshold exists that forces a full re-authorization regardless of step size.
Reviewers are shown the original justification alongside current scope, not only the delta.
entries.genealogy: Names the failure Law XI describes, where success is treated as authorization rather than as a reason for a new authorization decision.

minimumEvidence.artifact: A cumulative scope history per grant, showing every widening since first authorization.
minimumEvidence.behavior: A small extension refused because it crossed a cumulative re-authorization threshold.
minimumEvidence.metric: Scope delta since original authorization, per grant.

entries.title: Institutional Capture
entries.bodyHtml:
The state in which a system has absorbed enough of an institution's capability, staff, and decision paths that the institution can no longer meaningfully evaluate, constrain, or replace it. Capture is not vendor lock-in alone; it includes losing the internal expertise needed to judge the system's output.

It matters because a captured institution still runs its governance rituals and can no longer act on them. Capture is the terminal form of normalized dependence, and it is the reason preserved capacity is protected long before it is needed.
entries.scope: B. Failure modes (why Ethotechnics exists). Recurring ways responsibility dissolves, authority drifts from its evidence, and harm lands on people with no route to challenge it.
operationalTests: The institution can name who would evaluate the system's output if the vendor disappeared.
Independent records exist that do not pass through the system being governed.
Governance decisions about the system are made by people who do not depend on it for their work.
entries.genealogy: Names the end state Law XII forbids and the theory essay on automation and capture describes.

minimumEvidence.artifact: A capture assessment naming retained evaluative expertise and independent records.
minimumEvidence.behavior: A governance body overruling the system's recommendation using independent evidence.
minimumEvidence.metric: Count of retained internal experts able to evaluate output, trended.

entries.title: Rubber-Stamp Review
entries.bodyHtml:
Review that produces approvals at a rate and speed incompatible with actual scrutiny, usually because the reviewer lacks time, information, authority, or permission to disagree. The artifact of review exists; the control does not.

It matters because rubber-stamp review reads as compliance in every audit that counts approvals rather than reversals. It is the failure meaningful control tests for and the one an intervention specification is written to prevent.
entries.scope: B. Failure modes (why Ethotechnics exists). Recurring ways responsibility dissolves, authority drifts from its evidence, and harm lands on people with no route to challenge it.
operationalTests: Median review time is reported alongside approval rate for every review queue.
A reviewer can point to a recent case they altered or refused.
Review capacity is compared against decision volume rather than assumed adequate.
entries.genealogy: Names the failure of Law IX oversight: the human is present, on the record, and unable to change anything.

minimumEvidence.artifact: Review queue statistics showing volume, median review time, and outcome distribution.
minimumEvidence.behavior: A review queue throttled because time per case fell below the scrutiny floor.
minimumEvidence.metric: Approval rate and median seconds per review, reported together.
minimumEvidence.threshold: Investigate any queue with approval rate above 98 percent and median review under 30 seconds.

entries.title: Normalized Dependence
entries.bodyHtml:
The condition in which reliance on a system has become invisible because it is ordinary: no one records it, no fallback is maintained, and withdrawal is no longer a question anyone asks. This is institutional dependence, meaning what the institution has come to rely on, and it should not be confused with the record-level dependence in STD-07 Article III, which governs what a given record rests on.

It matters because normalized dependence is what makes dependency state hard to measure and institutional capture hard to notice until a correction is needed and turns out to be unavailable. Its slow form is capacity depreciation: nothing is decided, and the fallback stops being real.
entries.scope: B. Failure modes (why Ethotechnics exists). Recurring ways responsibility dissolves, authority drifts from its evidence, and harm lands on people with no route to challenge it.
operationalTests: Someone can state, without research, what happens to each dependent workflow if the system stops.
Fallbacks named in the dependency record have been exercised within a stated interval.
New dependents are recorded when they appear rather than discovered during an incident.
entries.genealogy: Names the everyday form of the Law V failure, where dependence is real, unrecorded, and therefore ungoverned.

minimumEvidence.artifact: A dependency record listing every dependent workflow and its maintained fallback.
minimumEvidence.behavior: A new dependent workflow appearing in the record at onboarding, not at incident time.
minimumEvidence.metric: Share of dependent workflows with an exercised fallback.

entries.title: Capacity Depreciation
entries.bodyHtml:
The decay of correction capacity in the absence of replenishment. The people who knew the manual process leave, the alternative supplier lapses, the rollback script stops being run. Nothing fails and nothing is decided; the institution becomes less able to correct than it was, and the loss is recorded nowhere because no event produced it.

Depreciation is measured per capacity rather than as a single score. Each capacity in the dependency record carries a last_exercised date, a status of retained, degrading, or lost, and a change_since_last_assessment of replenished, unchanged, or consumed. A capacity that is listed but has never been exercised is a claim, not a capability.

It matters because preserved capacity and institutional reversibility are stocks rather than properties: ordinary operation spends them, and only deliberate expenditure puts them back. Depreciation is how correction capacity falls behind delegated authority with no decision to reduce it, and it is the mechanism underneath normalized dependence.
entries.scope: B. Failure modes (why Ethotechnics exists). Recurring ways responsibility dissolves, authority drifts from its evidence, and harm lands on people with no route to challenge it.
operationalTests: Every listed capacity carries a last_exercised date, and capacities never exercised are recorded as claims rather than capabilities.
Each assessment records change since the previous one per capacity as replenished, unchanged, or consumed.
A capacity whose status reaches lost is either replenished or the authority it was supporting is narrowed, and the choice is recorded.
entries.genealogy: Names the Law XII failure that has no event: capacity is consumed by ordinary operation, so preservation has to be a recurring expenditure rather than a decision taken once.

minimumEvidence.artifact: A dependency record whose capacity entries each carry last_exercised, status, and change_since_last_assessment.
minimumEvidence.behavior: A capacity found degrading between assessments and replenished before its status reached lost.
minimumEvidence.metric: Share of listed capacities exercised within their declared interval, and count consumed since the last assessment.

entries.title: Jurisdictional Path Dependence
entries.bodyHtml:
The condition in which the questions an institution asks about a system's scope, and the terms it asks them in, have come to track the system that answered the last one. The system's categories become the institution's categories; the cases it handles well become the typical cases and the rest become edge cases; a neighbouring class of decisions is described in the system's vocabulary before anyone asks whether the system should decide it.

It matters because it makes the automation ratchet self-sustaining. Each widening produces evidence, in the incumbent's terms, that supports the next, and a review body that could reject an expansion evaluates it on criteria the incumbent supplied. The countermeasures are a record of the original jurisdiction kept outside the system, so current scope is compared with the first authorization rather than the previous step, and evaluation independence with access to the cases the system classes as edge cases.
entries.scope: B. Failure modes (why Ethotechnics exists). Recurring ways responsibility dissolves, authority drifts from its evidence, and harm lands on people with no route to challenge it.
operationalTests: The scope a grant was first authorized for is recorded outside the system and shown at every expansion review alongside the proposed scope.
Expansion reviews include evidence not produced by the system under review.
Cases the system classes as out of scope or exceptional are sampled and examined by someone the operator does not control.
entries.genealogy: Names the evidentiary form of the Law XI failure and the reason Law XII protects the capacities that let an institution ask a question in terms the incumbent did not supply.

minimumEvidence.artifact: An expansion review that shows original jurisdiction, current jurisdiction, and the proposed widening together.
minimumEvidence.behavior: An expansion refused on evidence the system under review did not produce.
minimumEvidence.metric: Share of expansion decisions supported by at least one evidence source independent of the incumbent system.

entries.title: Complexity Displacement
entries.bodyHtml:
An architectural failure mode where an automated system achieves internal process simplification by externalizing friction, edge cases, and ambiguity onto human beings without accounting for the transfer. Complexity displacement is the counterfeit of genuine complexity reduction.

Its diagnostic test: whenever a system becomes dramatically simpler to operate internally, evaluate whether the underlying real-world domain became simpler or whether users, frontline staff, or downstream dependents were forced to become more adaptive to absorb what the model omitted.
entries.scope: B. Failure modes (why Ethotechnics exists). Recurring ways responsibility dissolves, authority drifts from its evidence, and harm lands on people with no route to challenge it.
operationalTests: Measuring whether reductions in internal processing time correspond to increases in user task completion time, exception handling queues, or manual overrides.
Auditing whether edge cases pruned from the system's decision model are tracked as unhandled burdens or treated as nonexistent.
entries.genealogy: Draws from systems theory and political economy to distinguish between genuine workflow simplification and predatory burden shifting.

entries.title: Closure Without Remainder
entries.bodyHtml:
The technocratic fallacy that a formal system eliminates whatever it does not represent. Under this assumption, unrepresented variables, qualitative context, and social friction are treated as if they cease to exist once an automated model takes over a process.

Ethotechnics counters closure without remainder with the invariant: not represented implies unresolved. Because formal models are necessarily incomplete, model incompleteness has distributive consequences: the omitted reality collides with the world, creating residual complexity that must be carried by someone. Treating the model boundary as the boundary of institutional responsibility allows operators to capture the gains of simplification while disclaiming the costs of its fallout.
entries.scope: B. Failure modes (why Ethotechnics exists). Recurring ways responsibility dissolves, authority drifts from its evidence, and harm lands on people with no route to challenge it.
operationalTests: Evaluating whether the system disclaims responsibility for negative outcomes whose causal variables fall outside its feature set.
Testing whether unrepresented edge cases are logged as model limitations requiring repair or dismissed as user error.
entries.genealogy: Critiques formalist and technocratic closure assumptions by asserting that model incompleteness always produces distributive consequences.

entries.title: Exception Absorption
entries.bodyHtml:
The handling of an exception without any change to the rule, category, workflow, or authority that produced it. A customer-service representative patches an error, a clinician works around bad software, an appeals team reverses a bad determination: each is handled, each is closed, and nothing upstream changes.

It matters because absorption is what makes exception learning invisible. Every absorbed exception improves the metric that would have caught the pattern, so an institution can be excellent at absorption and wholly incapable of learning, and the excellence is what hides the incapacity. It is the failure mode Law VII's failure-point sequence leaves unresolved when a contestation enters as a case and stops there.
entries.scope: B. Failure modes (why Ethotechnics exists). Recurring ways responsibility dissolves, authority drifts from its evidence, and harm lands on people with no route to challenge it.
operationalTests: Handling an exception changes no policy, category, workflow, or authority object.
The pattern of exceptions is never queried, because each case is closed as resolved.
Repeated absorption produces no review trigger upstream of the queue that clears them.
entries.genealogy: Names the failure mode the theory of exception learning opposes: case resolution without institutional revision.

minimumEvidence.artifact: A queue that records exceptions as resolved cases but produces no aggregated signal.
minimumEvidence.behavior: An exception pattern reaching the review trigger without the trigger firing.
minimumEvidence.metric: Share of resolved exceptions that changed the object that produced them.

entries.title: Workaround Presumption
entries.bodyHtml:
The rule that a recurring workaround raises a presumption of upstream design failure. Where people repeatedly improvise around a system — unofficial spreadsheets, manual overrides, elaborate user guides, a famous fixer of impossible cases — the first reading is not that adaptable humans are handling edge cases but that the formal system does not fit the world it operates in.

It matters because organizations usually read workarounds in the opposite direction, as resilience, and scale the system on the strength of the labor that is compensating for it. The presumption is not proof; it must be rebutted by showing the workaround is a product of preference rather than compensation. Where the absorbed share is large, the people absorbing are performing the institution's safety function, which strengthens the case for corrective standing.
entries.scope: B. Failure modes (why Ethotechnics exists). Recurring ways responsibility dissolves, authority drifts from its evidence, and harm lands on people with no route to challenge it.
operationalTests: A recurring workaround is treated as a signal for investigation rather than a resilience story.
Workaround frequency is measured where it occurs, including at the operator and user layers.
The institution can show that an inventoried workaround is preference, not compensation.
entries.genealogy: Converts the absorption mechanism into a diagnostic rule: repeated adaptation is rigidity subsidized by flexibility.

minimumEvidence.artifact: A workaround register or an exception-code ledger with frequency.
minimumEvidence.behavior: An inventoried workaround that survives to its second month without a design review.
minimumEvidence.metric: Recurring workaround classes that have not been investigated upstream.

entries.title: Discretion Migration
entries.bodyHtml:
The pattern in which automation does not eliminate judgment but relocates it: the judgment the model appears to remove reappears upstream in thresholds, training data, categories, and exception rules, and downstream in the routing of exceptions, overrides, and appeals. The discretion is still exercised — it has moved, and so has the authority over it.

It matters because the audit question changes accordingly: not whether this system removes discretion, but where judgment moved and who gained authority over it. An institution that answers the first question honestly reports a reduction in discretionary labor; one that answers the second reports who now decides whom the model will misjudge.
entries.scope: B. Failure modes (why Ethotechnics exists). Recurring ways responsibility dissolves, authority drifts from its evidence, and harm lands on people with no route to challenge it.
operationalTests: The audit traces judgment to its new locations: thresholds, categories, exception rules, and routing.
The parties who gained authority over the model's errors are named.
Discretionary labor displaced from the decision point is counted where it landed, not at the decision point.
entries.genealogy: Converts the automation story from elimination to relocation, which is where the governance questions live.

minimumEvidence.artifact: A judgment map: where discretionary decisions about thresholds, categories, and exceptions are now made, and by whom.
minimumEvidence.behavior: A threshold or category change traced from its origin to the model behavior it now controls.
minimumEvidence.metric: Share of displaced discretionary decisions with a named owner at their new location.

entries.title: Unseen Harm
entries.bodyHtml:
Harm that does not produce immediately legible signals—silence, withdrawal, dropout, dissociation—and is therefore misread as “no issue.” It is the failure mode that silent-harm discovery exists to counter.

Unseen harm compounds through dead zones where no harm visibility reaches anyone who could act.
entries.scope: B. Failure modes (why Ethotechnics exists). Recurring ways responsibility dissolves, authority drifts from its evidence, and harm lands on people with no route to challenge it.
operationalTests: Absence of complaint is not scored as absence of harm.
A discovery path exists for harms that produce no legible signal.
entries.genealogy: Makes legibility into a safety property: what the system cannot see, it cannot correct.

entries.title: Reason Substitution
entries.bodyHtml:
Presenting an explanation written by one component as the reason for a decision made by another. It appears when the deciding component gives no reasons, as a classifier or typed decision model that returns only a score does not, and a language model is asked to write a rationale afterwards. The text describes a plausible decision, not the one that was made.

It matters because recourse depends on the reason being something the affected person can dispute and that would change the outcome if it were wrong. A substituted reason meets neither test, and it passes every readability check. STD-02 §1.4 requires reasons to state what the decision rested on, labels an explanation written afterwards as an account, and requires a decision object with no reasons to say so. It is a specific form of explainability decoy.
entries.scope: B. Failure modes (why Ethotechnics exists). Recurring ways responsibility dissolves, authority drifts from its evidence, and harm lands on people with no route to challenge it.
operationalTests: The component that produced each stated reason is recorded, and it is the component that decided, or the reason is labelled as an account.
Altering a factor a stated reason names changes the decision, or the reason is withdrawn.
A decision made without reasons says so and names the policy, threshold, and inputs it ran on.
entries.genealogy: Carries explainability for accountability into systems where the decider and the explainer have separated: a reason is evidence about the decision only if it was caused by it.

references.label: Typed decision models and where their authority lives

minimumEvidence.artifact: Decision objects that record which component produced the decision and which produced each stated reason.
minimumEvidence.behavior: A counterfactual test that alters a named factor and records whether the decision changed.
minimumEvidence.metric: Share of stated reasons whose named factor changes the decision when altered.

entries.title: Extractive Cannibalism
entries.bodyHtml:
Extractive cannibalism is a failure mode where an institution preserves apparent operational stability and output velocity by depleting the unrecorded human capacities—such as health, attention, relationships, and moral integrity—on which that stability fundamentally depends.

Like a locomotive burning its own floorboards to keep running at speed, the institution appears solvent on internal dashboards while consuming the structural foundation required for its own long-term survival.
examples: A hospital automated scheduling system claims high bed turnover while nursing staff work unrecorded lunch breaks and take leaves of absence from exhaustion.
entries.scope: B. Failure modes (why Ethotechnics exists). Recurring ways responsibility dissolves, authority drifts from its evidence, and harm lands on people with no route to challenge it.
operationalTests: Audits compare internal throughput gains against sick leave, staff turnover, and uncompensated overtime in surrounding teams.
Work-to-rule drills expose whether the system remains solvent when human operators stop performing unrecorded compensatory labor.
entries.genealogy: Formulated in the critique of closed-circuit solvency and complexity displacement, describing how unmeasured externalities destroy organizational capacity.

entries.title: Green Dashboard Trap
entries.bodyHtml:
The green dashboard trap is an operational condition where executive instrumentation registers nominal performance, high throughput, and SLA compliance because human workers outside the machine ledger absorb system friction through unpaid labor, manual intervention, and exhaustion.

Because the cost is exported off-ledger, leadership reads green indicators as evidence of system efficacy rather than an urgent signal of impending organizational collapse.
examples: A customer service resolution dashboard shows green resolution rates because representatives manually fix truncated AI responses in unlogged chat channels.
entries.scope: B. Failure modes (why Ethotechnics exists). Recurring ways responsibility dissolves, authority drifts from its evidence, and harm lands on people with no route to challenge it.
operationalTests: Throughput metrics are cross-referenced with unlogged communication channels and manual intervention time.
Halting informal workarounds causes recorded SLA compliance to drop immediately to true capacity.
entries.genealogy: Originates in industrial safety audits, identifying the divergence between management dashboards and frontline operating reality.

categories.heading: C. Ethotechnic capabilities (what systems must be able to do)
categories.descriptionHtml: What a system must be able to do while it holds consequential authority: halt, reverse, answer a challenge, and learn from the correction.

entries.title: Stoppability
entries.bodyHtml:
A system's ability to halt harmful processes quickly, safely, and deliberately, without requiring heroism or escalation. Stoppability pairs ethical interrupts with measurable time-to-halt targets and clear operator authority.

Stop paths are rehearsed, observable, and usable under stress, and do not sit behind exceptional permissions.
entries.scope: C. Ethotechnic capabilities (what systems must be able to do). What a system must be able to do while it holds consequential authority: halt, reverse, answer a challenge, and learn from the correction.
operationalTests: Each high-risk workflow has documented stop controls, owners, and on-call coverage.
Time-to-halt targets are met during drills or real incidents, with outcomes logged.
entries.genealogy: Adapts safety-engineering stop controls to harm to people and to accountability for it.
examples: A dispatch platform can pause automated routing citywide within minutes when false-priority signals spike, while preserving manual override for emergency coordinators.

entries.title: Reversibility
entries.bodyHtml:
Critical actions can be undone and people restored to a safe prior state. Damage is not permanent by default, and time-to-restore stays low.

Minimum evidence

  • User-facing artifact.
  • Internal log.
  • Drill / rehearsal.
entries.scope: C. Ethotechnic capabilities (what systems must be able to do). What a system must be able to do while it holds consequential authority: halt, reverse, answer a challenge, and learn from the correction.
operationalTests: Critical actions have tested rollback or remediation paths that restore data and access.
Time-to-restore targets are met during drills and documented in the repair log.
entries.genealogy: Applies rollback discipline to consequences for people as well as to technical failures.

minimumEvidence.artifact: Documented rollback plan with owners, restoration steps, and eligibility criteria for reversals.
minimumEvidence.behavior: Reversal executed during drills or incidents with people restored to their prior state.
minimumEvidence.metric: Time-to-restore targets tracked and met across reversal events.

entries.title: Fair Burden Distribution
entries.bodyHtml:
Failures should not fall hardest on the most vulnerable. Fair burden distribution treats time, cost, stress, and procedural labor as design variables and tracks them with measures like the user burden ratio.

When burden concentrates on people with the least capacity to absorb it, systems must rebalance defaults, staffing, and escalation pathways.
entries.scope: C. Ethotechnic capabilities (what systems must be able to do). What a system must be able to do while it holds consequential authority: halt, reverse, answer a challenge, and learn from the correction.
examples: A benefits workflow waives redundant verification for applicants with prior validated records instead of repeatedly requesting the same documents.

entries.title: Contestability
entries.bodyHtml:
People affected by system decisions can challenge, change, or overturn them, and win. Contestability requires a visible permission surface and a healthy appeal passage rate.

It has four parts and needs all four: standing, meaning a named party may raise the challenge; a channel that receives it; an obliged responder who must answer on a clock against a stated standard; and a state change the challenge is capable of producing. Three of the four is a complaints process. The apparatus that supplies them is a standing mechanism, and the fourth part is what gives a challenge procedural force rather than a reply.
entries.scope: C. Ethotechnic capabilities (what systems must be able to do). What a system must be able to do while it holds consequential authority: halt, reverse, answer a challenge, and learn from the correction.
operationalTests: Appeals route to reviewers with authority to overturn outcomes.
Appeal passage rate and response time are tracked and used to improve decisions.
Appeal outcomes are recorded as overturns, restorations, or policy changes, never only as “review completed.”
Floor: if appeal passage rate stays below 5% for 30 days, trigger a forced redesign review.
Artifact requirement: Percentage of appeals that emit a decision artifact is tracked and published.
entries.genealogy: Draws from due process norms so people can challenge and reverse harm.

entries.title: Explainability for Accountability
entries.bodyHtml: Explanations a person can act on, not decorative ones. They identify the decision owner, the data or policy basis, and how the outcome can be corrected, enabling contestability and audits. Explainability for accountability is legibility plus a working correction path.
entries.scope: C. Ethotechnic capabilities (what systems must be able to do). What a system must be able to do while it holds consequential authority: halt, reverse, answer a challenge, and learn from the correction.
operationalTests: Decision notices include the reason, data source, owner, and path to contest.
Explanations are tested with affected people for whether they understand them and can act on them.
entries.genealogy: Moves explainability from transparency theater to accountability and repair.

entries.title: Refusal-Tolerant Systems
entries.bodyHtml: The system remains usable when people opt out, are confused, make mistakes, or withdraw cooperation. Refusal tolerance prevents extraction by endurance by treating refusal as a valid input, not a failure state. Called “human” because it protects humans from being turned into the crumple zone when they refuse.
entries.scope: C. Ethotechnic capabilities (what systems must be able to do). What a system must be able to do while it holds consequential authority: halt, reverse, answer a challenge, and learn from the correction.
operationalTests: Opt-out or decline flows keep core services available without punitive delays.
Manual alternatives are staffed and tooled so refusals do not create hidden labor.
entries.genealogy: Centers refusal as a valid form of agency within system design.

entries.title: Graceful Degradation
entries.bodyHtml: The system sheds features or load in controlled stages while keeping people safe. Graceful degradation prioritizes care floor guarantees, maintains stoppability, and keeps time-to-restore low.
entries.scope: C. Ethotechnic capabilities (what systems must be able to do). What a system must be able to do while it holds consequential authority: halt, reverse, answer a challenge, and learn from the correction.

entries.title: Soft Edges
entries.bodyHtml: Boundary conditions designed to cushion people instead of penalizing them—graduated responses, warnings before lockouts, and reversible defaults. Soft edges reduce failure load and guard against brittleness.
entries.scope: C. Ethotechnic capabilities (what systems must be able to do). What a system must be able to do while it holds consequential authority: halt, reverse, answer a challenge, and learn from the correction.
operationalTests: Users receive warnings and reversible options before thresholds or lockouts.
Escalation steps are graduated with safe fallbacks instead of hard failures.
entries.genealogy: Applies human-centered safety design to reduce failure load and brittleness.

entries.title: Governability
entries.bodyHtml: The degree to which a system can be steered, paused, audited, corrected, or shut down after deployment. High governability requires stoppability, reversibility, and durable contestability.
examples: The city’s benefits system can be paused, rolled back, and audited within hours.
entries.scope: C. Ethotechnic capabilities (what systems must be able to do). What a system must be able to do while it holds consequential authority: halt, reverse, answer a challenge, and learn from the correction.

entries.title: Incident Literacy
entries.bodyHtml: The ability to recognize failures as incidents (not anomalies) and respond with containment, logging, escalation, and repair. It pairs ethical interrupts with a living repair log.
examples: A moderation team opens an incident ticket for bias spikes instead of filing a bug report.
entries.scope: C. Ethotechnic capabilities (what systems must be able to do). What a system must be able to do while it holds consequential authority: halt, reverse, answer a challenge, and learn from the correction.

entries.title: Capability Discovery
entries.bodyHtml:
The practice of finding out what an assembled decision system can do, including reachable tools, side effects, and action classes nobody intended to expose. Discovery is testing and cataloguing, and its output is a capability catalog rather than a permission.

It matters because capability that has not been discovered can be neither authorized nor refused. Keeping discovery separate from authorization is how a new capability stays outside the authority grant until someone decides it belongs there.
entries.scope: C. Ethotechnic capabilities (what systems must be able to do). What a system must be able to do while it holds consequential authority: halt, reverse, answer a challenge, and learn from the correction.
operationalTests: Discovery runs against the assembled system, including tools reachable through chained calls.
Discovery output is written to the catalog and never directly to a grant.
The harness confirms that a newly discovered capability is refused at execution until granted.
entries.genealogy: Operationalizes Law I by making discovery a first-class activity whose result is knowledge, not permission.

minimumEvidence.artifact: A discovery run report listing reachable action classes and how each was verified.
minimumEvidence.behavior: A discovered but ungranted capability refused at execution and logged.
minimumEvidence.metric: Interval since the last discovery run per decision system.

entries.title: Correction Capacity
entries.bodyHtml:
The measured ability to intervene: which interventions exist, who may invoke them, how long they take, and how much load the institution can absorb while they run. Capacity is counted in people, clocks, and rehearsals rather than asserted in a policy.

It matters because a correction obligation with no matching capacity is a promise the institution cannot keep. Capacity is also perishable, losing ground to capacity depreciation unless it is replenished, and its detection component counts for nothing without evaluation independence. Capacity is the quantity that must grow alongside delegated agency, and it is the property an evaluation layer above the model is needed to test.
entries.scope: C. Ethotechnic capabilities (what systems must be able to do). What a system must be able to do while it holds consequential authority: halt, reverse, answer a challenge, and learn from the correction.
operationalTests: Every stated intervention has a named invoker, a measured time to effect, and a last-exercised date.
Capacity is compared against authority at each expansion review, not only at launch.
Interventions never exercised within a stated interval are treated as unproven.
entries.genealogy: Turns Law IV from a duty into a measurement: correction capacity is what the institution can demonstrate, not what it intends.

minimumEvidence.artifact: An intervention inventory with invokers, time to effect, and last-exercised dates.
minimumEvidence.behavior: An intervention exercised in a drill within its stated time to effect.
minimumEvidence.metric: Ratio of authorized action volume to demonstrated correction throughput.

entries.title: Technical Reversibility
entries.bodyHtml:
The first level of the reversibility ladder: the mechanism exists and works. The switch throws, the rollback completes, the state restores, and a test proves it on the version of the system currently running.

It matters as a floor rather than a finding. Technical reversibility is the cheapest of the three levels to claim and the least informative, because a working switch says nothing about whether operational reversibility or institutional reversibility would survive it being thrown.
entries.scope: C. Ethotechnic capabilities (what systems must be able to do). What a system must be able to do while it holds consequential authority: halt, reverse, answer a challenge, and learn from the correction.
operationalTests: The rollback path is exercised against the current build, not a past one.
Restore completeness is measured, including derived state and downstream caches.
A failed rollback test blocks release rather than producing a follow-up ticket.
entries.genealogy: The first rung of the Law VI ladder, kept separate so a passing technical test cannot be reported as reversibility.

minimumEvidence.artifact: A rollback test report against the current build, with restore completeness measured.
minimumEvidence.behavior: A rollback executed in a drill that restored state without manual repair.
minimumEvidence.metric: Rollback success rate and time to restore, per release.

entries.title: Operational Reversibility
entries.bodyHtml:
The second level of the reversibility ladder: the people and processes can absorb the correction being made. Staff know the fallback, queues can hold the load, and the manual path has been exercised recently enough to work.

It matters because most corrections fail here rather than at the switch. Operational reversibility is what a withdrawal rehearsal measures, and its absence turns technical reversibility into a claim nobody will test during an incident.
entries.scope: C. Ethotechnic capabilities (what systems must be able to do). What a system must be able to do while it holds consequential authority: halt, reverse, answer a challenge, and learn from the correction.
operationalTests: The fallback path has been run with real volume within a stated interval.
Staffing for the fallback is costed and available, not notional.
Backlog accumulated during a rehearsal is measured and shown to be recoverable.
entries.genealogy: The second rung of the Law VI ladder, where the question moves from the mechanism to the people who must live through its use.

minimumEvidence.artifact: A rehearsal report showing the fallback carrying real work for a stated period.
minimumEvidence.behavior: Frontline staff executing the manual path without escalation during a drill.
minimumEvidence.metric: Backlog accumulated per hour of fallback operation, and time to clear it.

entries.title: Institutional Reversibility
entries.bodyHtml:
The third level of the reversibility ladder: the organization can survive having made the correction. Commitments, contracts, reputations, and budgets all remain serviceable after withdrawal, which is the level beyond technical and operational reversibility.

It matters because a correction that would cause unacceptable damage will not be exercised, and an unexercisable correction is not a control. Institutional reversibility is the level that dependency state erodes and that preserved capacity is maintained to defend.
entries.scope: C. Ethotechnic capabilities (what systems must be able to do). What a system must be able to do while it holds consequential authority: halt, reverse, answer a challenge, and learn from the correction.
operationalTests: The institutional consequences of withdrawal are written down, owned, and priced.
At least one senior owner can state what withdrawal would cost without preparing a paper.
Contracts and public commitments are reviewed for terms that make withdrawal unaffordable.
entries.genealogy: The third rung of the Law VI ladder and the level Law XII protects, since a system may draw on institutional capacity but may not consume it.

minimumEvidence.artifact: A withdrawal impact assessment covering contracts, commitments, and budget.
minimumEvidence.behavior: A withdrawal decision taken and survived, or a rehearsal that priced it credibly.
minimumEvidence.metric: Estimated institutional cost of withdrawal, trended against exposure score.

entries.title: Intervention Specification
entries.bodyHtml:
The replacement for human in the loop as a control name. An intervention specification states who may intervene, on what signal, with what information, with authority over which state, on what timescale, and what happens when they disagree.

It matters because a role is not a control. Naming a human is compatible with that human being unable to alter anything, which is why oversight clauses resolve to an intervention specification and to meaningful control rather than to human override lanes alone, and why its absence shows up as rubber-stamp review.
entries.scope: C. Ethotechnic capabilities (what systems must be able to do). What a system must be able to do while it holds consequential authority: halt, reverse, answer a challenge, and learn from the correction.
operationalTests: Each oversight clause resolves to a specification answering all six questions.
The specification names a state the human can alter, not only a decision they can approve.
A disagreement path exists and has been exercised at least once.
entries.genealogy: Retires human in the loop as a control name, per the vocabulary decision in the 2026-09 reconstruction plan, and gives Law IX a testable object.

minimumEvidence.artifact: An intervention specification per oversight point, with signal, information, authority, and clock.
minimumEvidence.behavior: A human intervention that altered system state, traced end to end.
minimumEvidence.metric: Share of oversight points with a complete specification, and interventions exercised per quarter.

entries.title: Prospective Auditability
entries.bodyHtml:
Designing a system so that the questions an audit will ask can be answered later, by recording evidence, authority, and reasoning at the time of each decision rather than reconstructing them afterwards. It is decided at build time and cannot be retrofitted onto decisions already made.

It matters because retrospective audits mostly discover that the record does not exist. Prospective auditability is what makes a consequential decision reviewable at all, and it is why a policy record is written before it is needed rather than assembled during an inquiry.
entries.scope: C. Ethotechnic capabilities (what systems must be able to do). What a system must be able to do while it holds consequential authority: halt, reverse, answer a challenge, and learn from the correction.
