entries.title: Moral Drift Control
entries.bodyHtml: Instrumentation that detects when a system’s behavior drifts from the baseline its authority was granted against, using MPIs or reports from affected people, and automatically triggers interrupts or design changes.
entries.scope: L. Future concepts / research areas. Open research threads: terms in use that do not yet carry operational tests or a minimum evidence standard.

entries.title: Structural Gentleness Coefficients
entries.bodyHtml: Measures of how much ordinary human variance an infrastructure tolerates before it fails someone: error tolerance, recovery time, and soft edges. Higher coefficients are expected to track lower failure load and safer degradation.
entries.scope: L. Future concepts / research areas. Open research threads: terms in use that do not yet carry operational tests or a minimum evidence standard.

entries.title: Burden Elasticity
entries.bodyHtml: How effort and risk move between parties when conditions change, and whether they move back afterward. Mapping burden elasticity alongside the burden gradient shows whether a crisis will land on the people with the least power to refuse it.
entries.scope: L. Future concepts / research areas. Open research threads: terms in use that do not yet carry operational tests or a minimum evidence standard.

entries.title: Care Redundancy
entries.bodyHtml: Overlapping routes through people, automated checks, and policy guarantees, so that when one safeguard fails another still catches the person. Care redundancy pairs with graceful degradation to keep failure load low.
entries.scope: L. Future concepts / research areas. Open research threads: terms in use that do not yet carry operational tests or a minimum evidence standard.

entries.title: Meta-Contestability
entries.bodyHtml: Mechanisms that let people challenge the rules of challenge as well as its outcomes: who may appeal, what evidence counts, and who sits on review panels. Meta-contestability keeps contestability from ossifying.
entries.scope: L. Future concepts / research areas. Open research threads: terms in use that do not yet carry operational tests or a minimum evidence standard.

entries.title: User-State Modeling for Harm Prevention
entries.bodyHtml: Inferring user states such as fatigue, distress, or inattention to slow the pace, add protective friction, or route to a person before harm compounds. The models must respect anticipatory consent and must not create new burden transfers.
entries.scope: L. Future concepts / research areas. Open research threads: terms in use that do not yet carry operational tests or a minimum evidence standard.

entries.title: Design for Ethical Latency
entries.bodyHtml: Designing for the unavoidable delay between an action and its review: staging risky steps, adding velocity friction, or holding care floor guarantees in place until the fuller review is done.
entries.scope: L. Future concepts / research areas. Open research threads: terms in use that do not yet carry operational tests or a minimum evidence standard.

entries.title: Distributed Accountability Protocols
entries.bodyHtml: Coordination methods that keep a named owner attached to work as it moves across teams and automation: shared playbooks, auditable handoffs, and repair logs. The protocols prevent accountability diffusion at the handoff.
entries.scope: L. Future concepts / research areas. Open research threads: terms in use that do not yet carry operational tests or a minimum evidence standard.

entries.title: Ethotechnic Failure Taxonomy
entries.bodyHtml: A shared classification of failure modes, such as optimization myopia, brittleness, and extraction, so incidents can be compared across systems, learned from, and prevented.
entries.scope: L. Future concepts / research areas. Open research threads: terms in use that do not yet carry operational tests or a minimum evidence standard.

entries.title: Adaptive Refusal Pathways
entries.bodyHtml: Flows that reroute a task when someone pauses or declines, keeping the case context and imposing no penalty. Adaptive pathways extend refusal budgets and strengthen refusal tolerance.
entries.scope: L. Future concepts / research areas. Open research threads: terms in use that do not yet carry operational tests or a minimum evidence standard.

entries.title: Aftercare Automation
entries.bodyHtml: Automated follow-up after an incident that checks on the people affected, schedules remedies, and prompts a named person to close the case. Done well, it lowers moral debt without adding moral overhead.
entries.scope: L. Future concepts / research areas. Open research threads: terms in use that do not yet carry operational tests or a minimum evidence standard.

entries.title: Alignment Dividend
entries.bodyHtml: The measurable gains in trust, retention, and safety when a system serves the people it acts on as intended. Tracking the dividend is the budget argument for sustained funding of MPIs and maintenance metabolism.
entries.scope: L. Future concepts / research areas. Open research threads: terms in use that do not yet carry operational tests or a minimum evidence standard.

entries.title: Ambiguity Budgets
entries.bodyHtml: Explicit allowances for uncertainty that hold back automation or strict enforcement until there is enough context. The budget reserves time, human review, or maintenance windows for the cases that need them.
entries.scope: L. Future concepts / research areas. Open research threads: terms in use that do not yet carry operational tests or a minimum evidence standard.

entries.title: Anticipatory Consent
entries.bodyHtml: Consent models that preview future data uses and let people pre-approve, defer, or block them. Anticipatory consent supports rights of exit and counters precision laundering of unclear terms.
entries.scope: L. Future concepts / research areas. Open research threads: terms in use that do not yet carry operational tests or a minimum evidence standard.

entries.title: Boundary of Acceptable Harm
entries.bodyHtml: Thresholds, revised as conditions change, that mark where harm exceeds the system’s mandate and operations must halt or escalate. Boundaries are tied to SLJs and enforced through ethical circuit breakers.
entries.scope: L. Future concepts / research areas. Open research threads: terms in use that do not yet carry operational tests or a minimum evidence standard.

entries.title: Care Floor Guarantees
entries.bodyHtml: Baseline commitments a service keeps during outages or crises: live support, data export, or safe defaults. Care floors protect users while graceful degradation is active.
entries.scope: L. Future concepts / research areas. Open research threads: terms in use that do not yet carry operational tests or a minimum evidence standard.

entries.title: Compassion Telemetry
entries.bodyHtml: Signals about how people are treated in an interaction: response tone, wait times during distress, and whether follow-up happened. They sit beside technical metrics and protect compassion bandwidth.
entries.scope: L. Future concepts / research areas. Open research threads: terms in use that do not yet carry operational tests or a minimum evidence standard.

entries.title: Conflict Observability
entries.bodyHtml: Logging that records a conflict between values when it happens, for example when SLJs are traded against throughput or appeals spike. The record lets the conflict be reviewed before it escalates and lets moral drift control start sooner.
entries.scope: L. Future concepts / research areas. Open research threads: terms in use that do not yet carry operational tests or a minimum evidence standard.

entries.title: Counter-Abuse Guardrails
entries.bodyHtml: Limits that stop tools from being repurposed for harassment, exploitation, or coercion: rate limits, anomaly detection, and human override lanes tuned for abuse cases.
entries.scope: L. Future concepts / research areas. Open research threads: terms in use that do not yet carry operational tests or a minimum evidence standard.

entries.title: Crisis Rehearsal Loops
entries.bodyHtml: Regular drills that test how a system responds to harm, as well as whether it stays up. They exercise ethical interrupts, check care floors, and record findings in the repair log.
entries.scope: L. Future concepts / research areas. Open research threads: terms in use that do not yet carry operational tests or a minimum evidence standard.

entries.title: Data Dignity Budgets
entries.bodyHtml: Caps on what data is collected and how it is used, set by context and purpose rather than by what a consent checkbox legally allows. Budgets align with anticipatory consent and guard against extraction.
entries.scope: L. Future concepts / research areas. Open research threads: terms in use that do not yet carry operational tests or a minimum evidence standard.

entries.title: Decision Debt Ledger
entries.bodyHtml: A register of deferred decisions and the harm each one accrues while it waits, reviewed before that harm compounds. The ledger feeds maintenance windows and informs MPIs.
entries.scope: L. Future concepts / research areas. Open research threads: terms in use that do not yet carry operational tests or a minimum evidence standard.

entries.title: Downstream Equity Buffers
entries.bodyHtml: Design slack that absorbs variance so marginalized groups do not pay first or most when errors occur. Buffers include staggered rollouts, rollback lanes, and targeted support funds.
entries.scope: L. Future concepts / research areas. Open research threads: terms in use that do not yet carry operational tests or a minimum evidence standard.

entries.title: Ethical Circuit Breakers
entries.bodyHtml: Automated stops that trip when a risk indicator crosses a set point: a surge in appeals, a bias metric, or rising moral debt. They are the safety counterpart to financial circuit breakers.
entries.scope: L. Future concepts / research areas. Open research threads: terms in use that do not yet carry operational tests or a minimum evidence standard.

entries.title: Ethical Load Testing
entries.bodyHtml: Exercises that probe how a system behaves when its safeguards are under stress, such as simulated harassment, mass appeals, or outages, to check that ethical circuit breakers trip and care floors hold.
entries.scope: L. Future concepts / research areas. Open research threads: terms in use that do not yet carry operational tests or a minimum evidence standard.

entries.title: Exhaustion Triggers
entries.bodyHtml: Signals that detect operator or user fatigue, such as error streaks, long queues, and late-night decisions, and automatically slow, pause, or hand off a flow before mistakes multiply. The triggers protect compassion bandwidth.
entries.scope: L. Future concepts / research areas. Open research threads: terms in use that do not yet carry operational tests or a minimum evidence standard.

entries.title: Friction Budgets
entries.bodyHtml: A planned allocation of protective and dignity friction across a workflow, set step by step according to risk, instead of removing friction wherever it slows things down.
entries.scope: L. Future concepts / research areas. Open research threads: terms in use that do not yet carry operational tests or a minimum evidence standard.

entries.title: Graceful Rollback Lanes
entries.bodyHtml: Prepared routes to revert harmful decisions while preserving dignity, evidence, and service continuity. Rollback lanes keep irreversibility indices low and shorten time-to-restore.
entries.scope: L. Future concepts / research areas. Open research threads: terms in use that do not yet carry operational tests or a minimum evidence standard.

entries.title: Harm Amnesty Windows
entries.bodyHtml: Time-boxed periods where people can report or reverse harmful actions without penalty, encouraging disclosure and faster repair. Amnesty windows often follow rehearsal loops or incidents.
entries.scope: L. Future concepts / research areas. Open research threads: terms in use that do not yet carry operational tests or a minimum evidence standard.

entries.title: Heat Maps of Refusal
entries.bodyHtml: Maps of where people opt out, churn, or appeal, which show early where refusal is being made costly. They are used to tune refusal budgets and redesign interaction surfaces.
entries.scope: L. Future concepts / research areas. Open research threads: terms in use that do not yet carry operational tests or a minimum evidence standard.

entries.title: Human Override Lanes
entries.bodyHtml:
Guaranteed routes for human judgment to supersede automation when stakes are high or context is missing. Override lanes accompany ethical interrupts and require clear ethical load paths.

A lane is a control only when it resolves to an intervention specification: who intervenes, on what signal, over which state, and by when. Without that, the lane names a person rather than establishing meaningful control.
entries.scope: L. Future concepts / research areas. Open research threads: terms in use that do not yet carry operational tests or a minimum evidence standard.

entries.title: Incident Memory Chains
entries.bodyHtml: Linked records that attach the findings from past incidents to the workflows most like them, so the next team sees them before repeating the failure. Memory chains inform ethical load tests and prevent moral lock-in on bad patterns.
entries.scope: L. Future concepts / research areas. Open research threads: terms in use that do not yet carry operational tests or a minimum evidence standard.

entries.title: Moral Dry Runs
entries.bodyHtml: Pre-launch walkthroughs that play out the hard cases a design will meet, such as conflicting obligations or a wrong decision nobody can reverse, before it reaches the public. Dry runs test circuit breakers, rollback lanes, and documentation.
entries.scope: L. Future concepts / research areas. Open research threads: terms in use that do not yet carry operational tests or a minimum evidence standard.

entries.title: Moral Feature Gating
entries.bodyHtml:
Controls that block a feature launch until readiness criteria are met: an oversight plan, a contestability pathway, a named incident owner, and minimum care floors. Moral feature gating makes those criteria a release requirement.

It prevents shipping features that work technically but that the institution cannot yet operate safely for the people they affect.
entries.scope: L. Future concepts / research areas. Open research threads: terms in use that do not yet carry operational tests or a minimum evidence standard.
examples: A personalization feature cannot launch until reversal paths, appeal handling capacity, and subgroup harm monitoring are verified.

entries.title: Pathways to Restitution
entries.bodyHtml: Documented steps a system must take to repair harm: acknowledgement, remedy, verification, and follow-up. Pathways reduce moral debt and belong in the repair log.
entries.scope: L. Future concepts / research areas. Open research threads: terms in use that do not yet carry operational tests or a minimum evidence standard.

entries.title: Refusal-Aware Routing
entries.bodyHtml: Routing logic that knows who can decline a task and makes sure a refusal is honored without retaliation or a silent penalty. It preserves refusal budgets so that declining stays a real option.
entries.scope: L. Future concepts / research areas. Open research threads: terms in use that do not yet carry operational tests or a minimum evidence standard.

entries.title: Relief Invariants
entries.bodyHtml: Guarantees that relief takes the same predictable effort and support whichever path a person comes in by. Relief invariants are tested in crisis rehearsals and anchored by care floors.
entries.scope: L. Future concepts / research areas. Open research threads: terms in use that do not yet carry operational tests or a minimum evidence standard.

entries.title: Repair Quorums
entries.bodyHtml: Minimum participation rules for authorizing fixes so impacted communities have a seat in deciding remedies. Repair quorums counter accountability diffusion and legitimize restitution.
entries.scope: L. Future concepts / research areas. Open research threads: terms in use that do not yet carry operational tests or a minimum evidence standard.

entries.title: Rest Cycle Enforcement
entries.bodyHtml: Built-in mechanisms that enforce rest and recovery—rotation policies, cooldown timers, enforced downtime—so fatigue does not translate into harm. Enforcement protects maintenance metabolism and compassion bandwidth.
entries.scope: L. Future concepts / research areas. Open research threads: terms in use that do not yet carry operational tests or a minimum evidence standard.

categories.heading: M. Foundational Ethotechnic principles
categories.descriptionHtml: The principles the method's laws and standards rest on.

entries.title: The Conservancy Principle
entries.bodyHtml: Designers hold the people a system affects and the resources it draws on in trust, and must leave systems safer and easier to repair than they found them. Conservancy prioritizes repair, stoppability, and reducing moral debt.
entries.scope: M. Foundational Ethotechnic principles. The principles the method's laws and standards rest on.

entries.title: The Burden Inversion Rule
entries.bodyHtml: When harm occurs, the system shoulders effort before the person harmed does. Burden inversion lowers the user burden ratio and demands rapid restoration.
entries.scope: M. Foundational Ethotechnic principles. The principles the method's laws and standards rest on.

entries.title: The Stop-Before-Explain Rule
entries.bodyHtml: Halt harmful behavior first, then justify or refine it. Systems must trigger ethical interrupts before offering explanations, preserving reversibility.
entries.scope: M. Foundational Ethotechnic principles. The principles the method's laws and standards rest on.

entries.title: The Maintenance Doctrine
entries.bodyHtml:
A system stays safe to rely on only while it is maintained: funded maintenance metabolism, scheduled maintenance windows, and transparent repair logs. Maintenance is a standing obligation, not a cleanup phase.

The doctrine requires institutions to budget for prevention, rehearsal, and repair before incidents force emergency tradeoffs.
entries.scope: M. Foundational Ethotechnic principles. The principles the method's laws and standards rest on.
examples: A product roadmap reserves recurring capacity for incident rehearsal and remediation work, protected from feature-priority overrides.

entries.title: The Principle of Low-Failure-Load Design
entries.bodyHtml: Design so that when failures occur, human impact is contained. This principle motivates graceful degradation, care floors, and low irreversibility indices.
entries.scope: M. Foundational Ethotechnic principles. The principles the method's laws and standards rest on.

entries.title: The Reversibility Mandate
entries.bodyHtml:
Critical actions must be undoable or paired with rollback lanes that can be exercised in real operating conditions. The mandate aligns with time-to-restore targets and contestability rights.

If reversal is impossible, systems should add explicit guardrails, higher review thresholds, and public ownership of residual risk.
examples: A benefits eligibility model deployment is blocked unless the team demonstrates a tested rollback path and a 24-hour restoration plan.
entries.scope: M. Foundational Ethotechnic principles. The principles the method's laws and standards rest on.

entries.title: The Contestability Guarantee
entries.bodyHtml: People affected by system decisions can challenge, change, or overturn them, and can win. Guarantees include wide permission surfaces, high appeal passage rates, and transparent design authority.
entries.scope: M. Foundational Ethotechnic principles. The principles the method's laws and standards rest on.

entries.title: Policy as State
entries.bodyHtml:
The rule that policy is a state of the running system rather than an input consumed at deployment. A policy record has a version, assumptions, an expiry, and a current status that other objects can read and react to.

It matters because policy held as a document cannot take part in control. Only policy held as state lets an assumption going stale change an authority grant without anyone remembering to look.
entries.scope: M. Foundational Ethotechnic principles. The principles the method's laws and standards rest on.
operationalTests: Policy status is queryable at runtime by the component that enforces authorization.
A policy change produces a state transition somewhere, or the change is recorded as non-binding.
No enforcement path depends on a human reading a policy document at the right moment.
entries.genealogy: States the second half of Law III as a design principle: policy is state, not input.

minimumEvidence.artifact: A runtime policy status endpoint or table that authorization checks read.
minimumEvidence.behavior: An authorization refused because the policy backing it was in a lapsed status.
minimumEvidence.metric: Share of enforceable policies with a machine-readable current status.

entries.title: Meaningful Control
entries.bodyHtml:
The condition under which a human is part of a control system: they can see the problem, hold authority to prevent or alter the action, have time to act, have a defined path when they disagree, and face incentives that permit disagreement. Anything less is presence, not control.

It matters because oversight is the most widely claimed and least evidenced control in deployed systems. Meaningful control is tested through an intervention specification, and its absence is what turns review into rubber-stamp review.
entries.scope: M. Foundational Ethotechnic principles. The principles the method's laws and standards rest on.
operationalTests: Reviewers can name the state they can change and the time budget they have to change it.
Disagreement has a defined route that does not depend on personal risk appetite.
Approval rates and reversal rates are both reported, not approval rates alone.
entries.genealogy: States Law IX as a principle a deployment either satisfies or does not, replacing the claim that a human is involved.

minimumEvidence.artifact: An oversight assessment answering the Law IX question set for each review point.
minimumEvidence.behavior: A reviewer halting or altering an action, with the trajectory change visible in logs.
minimumEvidence.metric: Reviewer-initiated state changes per thousand reviews, alongside median review time.

entries.title: The Non-Conversion Principle
entries.bodyHtml:
The rule that a fact about a system does not become a fact about its authority on its own. Capability, elapsed time without observed failure, and successful operation are evidence that a grant might be justified; none of them is a grant. Authority changes only through an explicit, recorded state transition, with the motivating fact attached as its basis. Confidence is a further instance: a high posterior about a person is evidence for a decision, never the authorization to act on them.

It matters because the conversions it refuses are the ones institutions make by default: a tool is reachable so it is used, a system has been quiet so it stays, a pilot went well so the rollout is not a decision. Laws I, II, and XI are the instances that matter most for delegated intelligence, and each is enforced by holding capability, evidence, and authority in different objects rather than by a rule of conduct. The authority grant and its state history are where a permitted conversion is written down.
entries.scope: M. Foundational Ethotechnic principles. The principles the method's laws and standards rest on.
operationalTests: Capability records and authority records are held in separate objects, and the first cannot write to the second.
Every widening or renewal of a grant appears as a recorded transition with a stated basis.
A capability that is reachable but not granted is refused, and the refusal is checkable by a harness.
entries.genealogy: Names the shape shared by Laws I, II, and XI, and argued for in the theory essay on what does not convert.

minimumEvidence.artifact: A grant whose state history shows each expansion and renewal as a transition with a recorded basis.
minimumEvidence.behavior: A reachable capability refused at execution because no grant covers it.
minimumEvidence.metric: Share of grant widenings that occurred as recorded transitions rather than being discovered after the fact.

entries.title: Post-Optimization Rigor
entries.bodyHtml:
The engineering posture required when mathematical optimization reaches its boundary. It acknowledges that optimizing any metric or reward function inevitably creates Goodhart drift, omits qualitative realities, and produces residual complexity.

Post-optimization rigor does not attempt to solve model incompleteness by endlessly adding more parameters or objective terms. Instead, it engineers the institutional architecture around the model: establishing independent review, measuring uncounted absorption, guaranteeing corrective standing to affected parties, and enforcing revocable authority grants.
entries.scope: M. Foundational Ethotechnic principles. The principles the method's laws and standards rest on.
operationalTests: The deployment pairs every optimized model with an independent correction and contestation infrastructure.
Performance audits track externalized friction and absorption rather than relying solely on internal loss functions or proxy metrics.
entries.genealogy: Defines the transition from model-centric optimization to socio-technical constitutional engineering.

entries.title: Human Non-Substitutability
entries.bodyHtml:
The ground rule that a model of a person is not the person: no representation, however accurate, acquires automatic authority to extinguish the represented person's standing against it. A system may infer, classify, predict, and recommend, but the person remains the party who carries the consequences and whose contestation the system must answer.

It matters because the framework's treatment of corrective standing rests on it. Standing is inalienable, not generous: if the subject of a decision could be replaced by a sufficiently detailed model of themselves, contestation would be a quality-control step a good enough model could close. Accuracy is evidence for a decision; it is never the decision, and it never substitutes for the person.
entries.scope: M. Foundational Ethotechnic principles. The principles the method's laws and standards rest on.
operationalTests: A system acting on an inference about a person can name what that person's challenge would do to the action.
Model accuracy is never cited as a reason a person's contestation is unnecessary.
The subject of a decision is identified separately from the user of the system.
entries.genealogy: The ground rule under Law VII, argued for in the theory of what a model of a person is and is not.

references.label: The model of a person is not the person

minimumEvidence.artifact: A decision record that names the person it acts on and the route by which that person can contest it.
minimumEvidence.behavior: A challenge by the represented person that reaches the inference that justified the action.
minimumEvidence.metric: Share of consequential decisions where the represented person's contestation route is recorded.

entries.title: Safe Incompleteness
entries.bodyHtml:
The design stance that a system should improve its representation of people and preserve their contestation at the same time, because the two capacities compound rather than substitute for each other. The error it opposes is closure without remainder: treating the model boundary as the boundary of relevance, so that every mismatch between the model and the person reads as user error, anomalous input, or noise.

It matters because a system that is incomplete and contestable is safer than one that is complete and final. The complete one has nowhere for its errors to arrive; the incomplete one constitutionalizes the failure path instead of optimizing it away, and the challenge route is the mechanism by which the representation's errors are discovered at all.
entries.scope: M. Foundational Ethotechnic principles. The principles the method's laws and standards rest on.
operationalTests: Better model performance is paired with preserved or widened contestation routes, not narrowed ones.
The system can state what its representation does not cover.
A mismatch between the model and the person can enter the system as an event with state-changing force.
entries.genealogy: The design consequence of closure without remainder: incompleteness is permanent, so contestability is the safety mechanism.

references.label: The model of a person is not the person

minimumEvidence.artifact: A stated coverage boundary: what the model represents, what it does not, and where challenges arrive.
minimumEvidence.behavior: A representation improvement shipped without narrowing any contestation route.
minimumEvidence.metric: Contestation route reach after each representation upgrade, compared with before.

entries.title: Anti-Conversion Rights
entries.bodyHtml:
The structural reading of rights as interruptions of illegitimate conversions: privacy interrupts the conversion of knowledge into action, due process interrupts the conversion of institutional position into outcome, consent rules interrupt the conversion of access into authority, appeal interrupts the conversion of decision into finality, and separation of powers interrupts the conversion of execution into evaluation.

It matters because it states what rights are for in Ethotechnic terms: not protections added around power, but the mechanisms that keep a capability from becoming an authorization. The non-conversion principle is the general form; the rights are its specific, historically won instances.
entries.scope: M. Foundational Ethotechnic principles. The principles the method's laws and standards rest on.
operationalTests: Each enumerated right on a deployment can be named as the conversion it interrupts.
A capability that a right blocks is recorded as unavailable, not as pending approval.
Removing a right would widen some authority surface, and that widening is named.
entries.genealogy: Extends the non-conversion principle from capability to the constitutional instruments that enforce it.

minimumEvidence.artifact: A rights-to-conversions map for the deployment: each right, and the capability it keeps from becoming authority.
minimumEvidence.behavior: An inference blocked from producing action because the right in question does not permit the conversion.
minimumEvidence.metric: Share of enumerated rights with a named conversion they interrupt.

entries.title: The Excluded Case
entries.bodyHtml:
The epistemological ground of institutional fallibilism: the case a representation excludes is potentially evidence about the category, not merely noise around it. A complaint can be knowledge. Repeated exception handling can reveal more about a system than its official performance metrics, because the exclusions are where the representation's boundaries become visible.

It matters because it is why dissent and standing are epistemic and not only political. Knowledge stays defeasible only if evidence the existing representation did not know how to recognize can still arrive — and it arrives through the people who carry it. That makes fallibilism material: a system is not meaningfully open to correction if the people who know it is wrong must destroy themselves to prove it, which is the condition corrigibility rent prices.
entries.scope: M. Foundational Ethotechnic principles. The principles the method's laws and standards rest on.
operationalTests: Cases outside the model's support can enter as challenges rather than being discarded as noise.
Exception patterns feed category review, not only case resolution.
The cost of raising an excluded case is measured against the challenger's capacity to bear it.
entries.genealogy: The fallibilist premise under exception learning and safe incompleteness: the residual is data, and who can afford to bring it decides whether the institution can know.

minimumEvidence.artifact: An exceptions register where out-of-support cases are recorded as potential category evidence.
minimumEvidence.behavior: An excluded case that produced a category or rule review rather than a case-level fix.
minimumEvidence.metric: Share of exception classes whose pattern reached a category or rule review.

entries.title: Feedback Proximity
entries.bodyHtml:
The design principle that the causal distance between an institutional error and the actors who can revise the generating rule should be kept as short as the stakes demand. Where error-bearing parties sit far from rule-makers (by hierarchy, by time, by evidence format, or by classification), corrections arrive late, weakened, or not at all.

It matters because proximity is not visibility. A harm can be fully visible to the people carrying it and still reach nobody who can change the rule that produces it. Shortening proximity means building the channels that let mismatch travel from the edge back to the rule: corrective standing, records that travel, and halt stratification. Insulation is distance from corrective consequence; feedback proximity is the commitment that shortens it.
entries.scope: M. Foundational Ethotechnic principles. The principles the method's laws and standards rest on.
operationalTests: A harm reported at the frontline reaches an actor who can change the generating rule through a bounded number of named hops.
The latency from first signal to rule revision is measured and bounded, not merely visible.
Error-bearing parties can state the shortest path from their report to a rule change, and that path exists.
entries.genealogy: The positive form of insulation: where insulation names distance from corrective consequence, feedback proximity names the design commitment to shorten that distance.

minimumEvidence.artifact: A mapped path from frontline signal to rule-revising authority, with named responders at each hop.
minimumEvidence.behavior: A reported mismatch that produced a rule change without an intervening heroic intervention.
minimumEvidence.metric: Time, or number of hops, from first signal to generating-rule revision, tracked per failure class.

entries.title: Asymmetric-Capacity Restraint
entries.bodyHtml:
The principle that an institution's obligations to remain contestable and revisable grow with its capacity to classify, monitor, automate, enforce, and scale. The more a system can see, sort, act on, and impose its categories, the stronger the counterweights must be.

It matters because capacity is not neutral. A system that can classify at scale can misclassify at scale, and a system that can enforce quickly can commit quickly. Restraint is the obligation side of capability overhang: capability may expand only as fast as the correction obligation that checks it. It is why earned autonomy is conditional rather than cumulative, and it makes Law XI's burden normative: every expansion of capacity carries a proportional expansion of contestation and revision.
entries.scope: M. Foundational Ethotechnic principles. The principles the method's laws and standards rest on.
operationalTests: Each expansion of classification, monitoring, or enforcement capacity is paired with a stated increase in contestation and revision capacity.
Correction capacity grows with authority, and the pairing is recorded rather than asserted.
A capability that outruns its correction capacity is refused admission or narrowed, not shipped and apologized for later.
entries.genealogy: The normative form of capability overhang: where overhang describes the mismatch, restraint names the obligation that prevents it.

minimumEvidence.artifact: A grant whose scope expansion is paired with a corresponding correction-capacity expansion, recorded in the same transition.
minimumEvidence.behavior: A capability refused or narrowed because its correction capacity was not yet provisioned.
minimumEvidence.metric: Ratio of correction capacity to granted authority, required non-decreasing across expansions.
